name: Carvana Co.

profile.description: Carvana operates the largest e-commerce platform for buying and selling used cars in the United States, combining online purchase and financing with in-house reconditioning, logistics, home delivery, car vending machines and the ADESA wholesale auction network. Q3 2026 revenue rose ~42% YoY to about $8.0B on ~217,000 retail units (+39%), following a record Q2 of $7.38B revenue and 197,325 units. The stock split 5-for-1 in May 2026, and the Garcia family controls more than 80% of the voting power. Headquartered in Tempe, Arizona.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Carvana built a fully online used-car buying model with vending-machine pickup, added ADESA wholesale auctions, and grew revenue from $5.59B in 2020 to $20.32B in 2025 while moving from deep losses to $1.41B of 2025 net income, a transformative execution record [3][1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Garcia has said AI will significantly affect the auto business, and Carvana uses AI for coding, chatbots and its instant 'Value Now' appraisal offers, but no quantified savings or AI revenue were found [5]. Market Share (2/2): Retail units grew 38% YoY in Q2 2026 and ~39% in Q3, which the company describes as industry-leading growth, making Carvana the fastest share gainer in US used-car retail [1][2]. Pipeline (1/2): Management guides to sequential unit growth and 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.7-3.0B, but no named next-generation products with dates surfaced [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Carvana reports no separate R&D expense; technology spend sits inside G&A [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Carvana's aim to change the way people buy and sell cars is specific and has shaped a decade of decisions, from vending machines to owning reconditioning and logistics, though it is not yet validated across decades [5][7]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable programs with quantified dollars were found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP data shows 4 open-market purchases against 41 sales in Q3 2026 and 102 sales with no purchases in Q2 2026, a clear net-selling pattern [8].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Growth-sleeve calculation: D/E 100.8% scores 0.87 (1x); ROE 54.7% scores 1.0 (2x); revenue growth 42.4% scores 1.0 (1x); 5-year revenue CAGR of 29.5% (2020 $5.59B to 2025 $20.32B, derived) scores 1.0 (2x); forward P/E 30.3 scores 0.74 (1x); profit margin 6.2% scores 0.31 (1x); FMP forward PEG 0.41 scores 1.0 (2x) [2][3][4]. Weighted sum 8.92 / 10 = 9. Note that 2025 net income included a ~$2.8B income-tax benefit, so trailing ROE and P/E flatter underlying earnings power; total debt is $5.70B against $3.61B of cash [2][3]. Liquidity floor cleared at ~8.6M shares x $68 = ~$588M daily.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Carvana's moat is physical: inspection and reconditioning centers, a national logistics network and ADESA auction sites that AI cannot replicate, and AI tools such as instant appraisal strengthen rather than replace that system [5][1]. The exposure is that AI agents and shopping assistants could commoditize the online car-shopping front end and make it easier for traditional dealers to match Carvana's digital experience. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue was identified; AI is an internal efficiency tool [5].

infinite_game.summary: Carvana has a real cause in reinventing car buying and survived a near-death 2022-2023 without abandoning its integrated model, which Sinek would credit. But founder-family control with centralized decision-making, recurring short-seller allegations about related-party dealings with DriveTime, and heavy insider selling keep it from reading as an organization built on a circle of safety.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Changing how people buy and sell cars is a service-oriented cause that has visibly driven strategy since 2012, including the decision to own reconditioning, logistics and auctions rather than run an asset-light marketplace [5][7]. It has survived one existential crisis but not a leadership transition, so it is partially proven.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept the capital-intensive ADESA network and integrated infrastructure through the 2022-2023 downturn, a bet that now underpins record volumes of ~217,000 units a quarter [1][2]. Offsetting this, the company's growth was financed with heavy leverage and the Garcia family has been a consistent seller [8].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Co-founder Ernie Garcia III has been CEO since 2012 and the company formalized its founder-era culture into written values as it scaled [5][7]. Analysts describe a functional structure with centralized decision-making under the CEO, and no employee retention data was found, so trust is scored as adequate.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Carvana moved from pure online retail into wholesale with ADESA and pivoted from growth-at-all-costs to profitability, swinging from a $1.59B loss in 2022 to $1.41B of 2025 net income [3]. These shifts adapted the model rather than abandoning a core business.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary acknowledging rivals' strengths was found; Carvana frames its results as 'industry-leading' growth against traditional dealers, a finite share-taking frame [1].

investment_thesis: Carvana is compounding at scale: Q2 2026 delivered record revenue of $7.38B (+52%), 197,325 retail units (+38%), $513M net income and a record $769M adjusted EBITDA at a 10.4% margin, and Q3 revenue grew ~42% to about $8.0B on ~217,000 units (+39%) [1][2]. Management guides 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $2.7-3.0B versus $2.24B in 2025, and the integrated reconditioning, logistics and ADESA footprint gives it a cost and selection advantage that is hard to replicate [1]. ROE of 54.7%, a forward P/E of 30 and a forward PEG of 0.41 point to growth that is still cheap relative to its pace [2][4].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on governance and earnings quality. Gotham City Research's January 2026 report alleged that Carvana moved more than $1B of expenses through undisclosed related-party dealings with DriveTime, controlled by the CEO's father, sending the stock down 14%; Carvana called it 'inaccurate and intentionally misleading' [6]. The Garcia family controls more than 80% of votes, the board need not be majority independent, and the audit committee chair is a long-time DriveTime banker [6]. Reported 2025 earnings included a ~$2.8B tax benefit, the 6.2% net margin leaves little cushion in a used-car downturn, and debt totals $5.70B [2][3].
key_catalysts: Delivery of full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA at the high end of the $2.7-3.0B guide with sequential retail-unit growth into Q4 2026 [1][2]
Continued share gains, with retail units growing ~39% YoY against a flat used-car market, as ADESA sites add reconditioning capacity [2]
Revenue growth aligning with unit growth from Q3 2026 as gross-revenue accounting effects fade, improving quality and comparability of reported growth [1]
key_risks: Regulatory or audit follow-up on Gotham City Research's allegation of more than $1B in related-party expense shifting to DriveTime [6]
Controlled-company governance: Garcia family >80% voting control, non-majority-independent board, and persistent insider selling [6][8]
Used-car credit and pricing cycle: a 6.2% net margin and $5.70B of debt leave limited cushion if subprime auto credit or used-vehicle prices deteriorate [2]
